items.title: A unique factorization domain satisfies the ascending chain condition for principal ideals
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a unique factorization domain satisfies the ascending chain condition for principal ideals (statement lines 29759-29763). The proof does not argue with divisor chains or invoke Noetherianity of any kind: it factors the first element of a given ascending chain as a product of primes, then uses the containment of principal ideals to see that every later element is an associate of a product of the same primes with exponents bounded by those of the first element, so only finitely many possibilities arise (proof lines 29765-29771). The finiteness of the exponent bookkeeping, driven entirely by unique factorization, is the content. H2.
